--- order: 8 unit: challenge optional: true assumes: [console-log, js-query, text-content] title: "The real browser console" summary: "Use console.log to look inside your page, read error messages, and try the real Console and inspector in your own browser." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 12 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "", zoom: 1.4} caption: "console.log shows what your code sees" say: "console dot log shows what your code sees." clip: - caption: text: "console.log writes messages in the Console, not on the page." say: "console dot log writes messages in the Console, not on the page." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "

Sports day

\n

Bring a hat.

\n

Bring water.

\n\n", append: true} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 750 - caption: "Two messages in the Console. The page itself did not change." - wait: 750 hook: "Web developers keep one window open all day to see what their code is really doing." --- The **Console** is a list of messages from your page. `console.log(...)` writes one, `console.warn(...)` writes a warning, and `console.error(...)` writes an error. When something goes wrong the browser writes its own red error there, with the line it happened on. `document.querySelectorAll("p")` finds **every** matching element, not just the first, and its `.length` says how many. The Console in this playground is a copy of the real one. Your browser has a **real** Console and an **inspector** on every web page: press **F12** (or right-click a page and choose **Inspect**), then open the **Console** tab. **The hard part** is reading the message. An error such as `cout is not defined` is telling you the name it could not find, and the line: read both before you change anything. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict check: type: predict q: "How many messages does the Console show?" options: ["4", "2", "1", "0"] actual: "4. There are two console.log lines, one console.warn and one console.error. Each writes a message in the Console, in its own style." ``` Count the console lines in the script. ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I ran the page and read the three messages in the Console." } ``` Press **Run** and look at the Console under the page. The script logs what it found: the heading, the first paragraph and its tag name. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "console.log shows what your code sees without changing the page, and an error message names the problem and the line, so read both." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each piece with what it does." pairs: - ["console.log(\"Heading:\", heading.textContent);", "writes a message with a label and the value"] - ["console.warn(\"Careful!\");", "writes a warning in the Console"] - ["document.querySelectorAll(\"p\").length", "how many paragraphs are on the page"] - ["document.querySelector(\"p\")", "the first paragraph only"] - check: type: question q: "The Console says \"ReferenceError: cout is not defined\" on line 6. What should you do first?" options: ["Look at line 6 for a name that is not spelled the same as one you made", "Delete the script", "Reload the page", "Add more console.log lines to every line"] answer: 0 explain: "The message names the word it does not know (cout) and the line. Compare it with the names you made: count is not cout." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "The Console shows \"cout is not defined\". Click the line where the Console says it happened." answer: 6 fault: runtime misconception: name-typo explain: "The variable is called count, but line 6 writes cout. JavaScript treats them as different names and cannot find the second." ``` ### Which piece does what? Log, warn and find. ### Reading an error Name and line. ### Spot the bug The Console tells you exactly where. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "querySelectorAll finds every match, and a loop can log each one." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } tasks: - hint: - "querySelector gives the first one. Is there a version that gives all of them?" - "const paragraphs = document.querySelectorAll(\"p\"); then console.log(paragraphs.length)." check: { type: code, text: "Log how many paragraphs the page has.", rules: { contains: ["querySelectorAll", ".length"] } } - hint: - "You already know a loop that visits every item of a list." - "for (const p of paragraphs) { console.log(p.textContent); }" try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#sol-count", height: 430 } check: { type: code, text: "Log the text of every paragraph, one message each.", rules: { contains: ["for (", "textContent"] } } ``` ### How many paragraphs? Find all, then count. ### Each paragraph A loop over the matches. ## Make: explore a page ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: use the Console to learn four facts about a page, then try the real Console in your own browser." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I used console.log to learn four things about a page, and I opened the real Console in my browser (F12 or Inspect) and tried document.title." } ``` Use `console.log` to find **four facts** about the page: its heading, how many paragraphs, how many have the class `note`, what the note says. Then open the real Console on any web page (press **F12**, or right-click and choose **Inspect**) and type `document.title` and press Enter. Changes you make there only last until you reload the page. **Never paste code into the Console because someone online told you to**: it runs with your accounts logged in. ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "You have finished the course. What is the best way to get better at making pages that react?" options: ["Make something you want, and use the Console to find out why it does not work yet", "Memorise every method", "Copy a whole page and never read it", "Avoid errors"] answer: 0 explain: "Making pages you care about, with the Console open, is how developers learn. Errors are information, not failure." ``` That is the end of the course. Next: your own project, the Python web apps course for pages that remember, or the p5.js course to draw and animate. ```teacher summary: Students use console.log, warn and error to look inside a page, find elements with querySelectorAll and count them, read an error message for its name and line, and try the real browser Console. time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 10 min · Make 15 min goals: - I can use console.log to see what my code is doing. - I can read an error message for the name and the line. - I can open my browser's Console and inspector. before: > Optional enrichment after the challenge. The playground's Console shows what `console.log`, `warn` and `error` write, and what the browser would say about an error, in plain words first. In the real browser, F12 (or right-click, Inspect) opens the DevTools; the Console tab is the same idea, with more tools. Check the school's browsers allow DevTools before the lesson: some managed devices block it, and the Make step then stays in the playground. Make a point of the safety rule: never paste code into the Console because someone told you to. Changes made in the real Console last until the page is reloaded and do not change the real site. running: - "Predict: ask students to count console lines before running." - "Run: ask where the messages appear and where they do not." - 'Investigate: for the bug, ask "what is the exact word it does not know?"' - "Modify: ask what querySelectorAll gives that querySelector does not." - "Make: if allowed, demonstrate F12 on the class page together." stuck: - see: Nothing appears in the Console. ask: Was Run pressed, and is there a console.log line? fix: Press Run and check the spelling of console.log. - see: X is not defined. ask: Is X spelled the same as the name you made? fix: Compare the two names letter by letter. - see: Cannot read properties of null. ask: Did the selector find anything? fix: Check the selector against the HTML. - see: F12 does nothing. ask: Is DevTools blocked on this device? fix: Use the playground Console instead; try right-click, Inspect. stretch: Use the real Console on a favourite site to find a heading with document.querySelector("h1").textContent, and change it to see the page change (until reload). support: Give the loop and ask students only for the labels in the messages. leads: "From here: students build their own page project, or move on to the Python web apps course." exit: q: What two things does an error message tell you? a: The word it could not make sense of, and the line it happened on. explain: | 1. `console.log(…)` writes a message in the Console, not on the page. 2. `querySelectorAll("p")` finds every paragraph; `.length` counts them. 3. An error names the problem and the line: read both first. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-count step-4#t2: page.html#sol-loop step-5: page.html#sol-make struggle: 'Reading the error word for word: it names what it could not find. Ask "what is the exact word, and where did you make it?"' ```
